title: Unconditional Advantage Of Quantum Teleportation Over Direct Transmission Of Single Photons Through A Lossy Channel
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 23 June 2026;
tldr: Experimental demonstration that quantum teleportation achieves higher efficiency than direct single-photon transmission through a lossy channel.
motivation: To determine whether quantum teleportation can provide an advantage in realistic lossy channels, which is crucial for quantum network design.
method: The authors perform a controlled experiment comparing the success probability of teleporting a photonic qubit versus directly transmitting a single photon through an identical lossy channel.
result: Quantum teleportation yields a higher success probability than direct transmission, demonstrating an unconditional advantage.
conclusion: Quantum teleportation can overcome loss in quantum communication channels, making it a key primitive for future quantum networks.

title: A Photonic Integrated Long-distance Quantum Communication Network
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: A photonic integrated quantum network using twin-field QKD over 540 km fiber with full connectivity between four users.
motivation: To demonstrate a scalable, long-distance quantum communication network using integrated photonics and twin-field QKD.
method: A four-user spine-leaf network architecture with twin-field QKD protocol operating at 1.25 GHz clock rate over up to 540 km fiber.
result: Achieved secret key rate of 9.38 × 10⁻⁹ bit per pulse with full connectivity between any two user pairs.
conclusion: The work shows the feasibility of integrated photonic quantum networks for long-distance secure communication.

title: Analytical Computation Of Entanglement Distribution Time In First-generation Quantum Repeater Chains
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 June 2026;
tldr: Analytical model for entanglement distribution time in first-generation quantum repeater chains, providing closed-form expressions and scaling laws.
motivation: Understanding the time required to distribute entanglement over long distances is crucial for designing efficient quantum repeater networks.
method: Derives analytical expressions for the entanglement distribution time by modeling the probabilistic processes of entanglement generation, swapping, and purification in a chain of repeater nodes.
result: Obtains closed-form formulas for the mean and variance of the distribution time, revealing scaling with chain length and key system parameters.
conclusion: The analytical model enables rapid evaluation of repeater chain performance without Monte Carlo simulations, aiding in the design of practical quantum networks.

title: Restoring Heisenberg Scaling In Time Via Autonomous Quantum Error Correction
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates that autonomous quantum error correction can restore Heisenberg-limited scaling in time for quantum sensing, overcoming standard quantum limit constraints.
motivation: Quantum sensing typically suffers from the standard quantum limit, and Heisenberg scaling is fragile under decoherence. The authors aim to achieve Heisenberg scaling in time using autonomous quantum error correction.
method: They propose a scheme where a sensor qubit is coupled to an ancilla qubit with engineered dissipation, implementing continuous error correction that protects the sensor from noise while preserving the scaling advantage.
result: The scheme achieves Heisenberg scaling in time for frequency estimation, with the error scaling as 1/T^2, where T is the total interrogation time, even in the presence of Markovian noise.
conclusion: Autonomous quantum error correction can restore Heisenberg scaling in time, offering a practical path to high-precision quantum sensing under realistic noise conditions.

title: Louvre: Relaxing Hardware Requirements Of Quantum Ldpc Codes By Routing With Expanded Quantum Instruction Set
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: Proposes a routing-based approach to relax hardware connectivity requirements for quantum LDPC codes using an expanded quantum instruction set.
motivation: Quantum LDPC codes promise low overhead but require high connectivity, which is challenging for near-term hardware. This work aims to reduce connectivity demands by introducing routing operations.
method: The authors design an expanded quantum instruction set that includes routing operations, enabling efficient mapping of LDPC code circuits onto hardware with limited connectivity. They analyze the trade-offs between routing overhead and code performance.
result: The proposed method significantly reduces the required hardware connectivity for implementing quantum LDPC codes, with only modest increases in circuit depth and qubit overhead.
conclusion: Routing with an expanded instruction set is a practical approach to make quantum LDPC codes more feasible on near-term quantum devices, advancing quantum network and error correction integration.

title: Three-outcome Multipartite Bell Inequalities: Applications To Dimension Witnessing And Spin-nematic Squeezing In Many-body Systems
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 13 June 2026;
tldr: Derives three-outcome multipartite Bell inequalities and applies them to dimension witnessing and spin-nematic squeezing in many-body systems.
motivation: To develop Bell inequalities beyond binary outcomes for multipartite systems, enabling new applications in dimension witnessing and quantum metrology.
method: Constructs Bell inequalities using three-outcome measurements and analyzes their violation in many-body spin systems, connecting to spin-nematic squeezing.
result: The inequalities provide tight bounds for quantum correlations and can be used to certify the dimension of the underlying Hilbert space and detect spin-nematic squeezing.
conclusion: Three-outcome Bell inequalities are a useful tool for characterizing quantum correlations in many-body systems, with practical applications in dimension witnessing and metrology.

title: Long-lived Photon Blockade With Weak Optical Nonlinearity
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 20 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates long-lived photon blockade using weak optical nonlinearity in a cavity QED system.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong nonlinearities; this work aims to achieve it with weak nonlinearities for practical quantum devices.
method: Uses a cavity QED setup with a weak Kerr nonlinearity and engineered dissipation to sustain photon blockade over long times.
result: Achieves long-lived photon blockade with significantly weaker nonlinearity than conventional approaches.
conclusion: Weak nonlinearities can be harnessed for quantum optical effects, broadening the range of platforms for quantum information processing.

title: Entanglement As A Fairness Mechanism In Randomized Quantum Games
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This paper proposes using entanglement as a fairness mechanism in randomized quantum games, showing that entangled strategies can ensure fair outcomes in competitive settings.
motivation: Classical randomized games often suffer from unfair advantages due to imperfect randomness or cheating. The authors aim to leverage quantum entanglement to enforce fairness without trusted third parties.
method: They design a quantum game framework where players share entangled states and perform measurements; fairness is quantified via payoff expectations and entanglement is used to prevent bias.
result: Entangled strategies can achieve fairer outcomes than any classical randomized strategy, and the fairness is robust against certain types of cheating.
conclusion: Entanglement serves as a resource for fairness in quantum games, with potential applications in quantum cryptography and distributed decision-making.

title: Multiple Photons Enhance Quantum Machine Learning
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates that using multiple photons in quantum machine learning can improve classification accuracy and robustness, with experimental validation on a photonic processor.
motivation: Quantum machine learning often relies on single-photon qubits, but noise and limited resources hinder performance. The authors explore whether multiple photons can enhance learning outcomes.
method: They implement a quantum kernel method on a photonic chip, encoding data into multiple photons and measuring interference patterns to compute kernel values. Experiments compare single-photon and multi-photon setups.
result: Multi-photon states yield higher classification accuracy and better noise resilience in supervised learning tasks, with theoretical bounds on the advantage.
conclusion: Multiple photons provide a practical resource for improving quantum machine learning, though the advantage is limited and depends on the task.

title: Emergent Partons In Fractional Quantum Hall Systems
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This paper reports experimental observation of multiple chiral spin-2 neutral excitations in fractional quantum Hall systems, providing evidence for the parton description.
motivation: To test the parton theory of the fractional quantum Hall effect by detecting predicted chiral spin-2 neutral excitations.
method: Experimental measurement of neutral excitations in fractional quantum Hall systems using optical or transport techniques.
result: Multiple chiral spin-2 neutral excitations were observed, supporting the parton model.
conclusion: The findings confirm the parton description of the fractional quantum Hall effect.

title: Nanoscale Strain Wave Generation By A Piezoelectric Grating From Polar Vortices
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates the generation of nanoscale strain waves using a piezoelectric grating formed by polar vortices, enabling diffraction of X-rays.
motivation: To create a tunable diffraction grating for strain waves at the nanoscale, leveraging polar vortex structures for piezoelectric modulation.
method: A periodic array of polar vortices in a ferroelectric material is used as a piezoelectric grating; upon applying an electric field, it generates coherent strain waves that diffract X-rays.
result: The piezoelectric grating produces nanoscale strain waves that act as a dynamic diffraction grating for X-rays, with tunable periodicity.
conclusion: This approach provides a new method for generating and controlling strain waves at the nanoscale, with potential applications in X-ray optics and nanophononics.

title: Microscopic Signatures Of An Imaginary Charge Density Wave In A Kagome Metal
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: Observation of microscopic signatures of an imaginary charge density wave with spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking in a kagome metal.
motivation: To experimentally confirm the existence of imaginary charge density waves and loop currents in kagome metals, which has been an open question.
method: Experimental measurements on CsV3Sb5 using techniques sensitive to time-reversal symmetry breaking.
result: Signatures of spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking consistent with an imaginary charge density wave were observed.
conclusion: The findings provide evidence for a novel quantum state in kagome metals, but the paper is focused on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Attosecond Tuning Of Coherent Electron Dynamics In Doped Semiconductors
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 12 June 2026;
tldr: Demonstrates sub-cycle light-field control of coherent electron dynamics in doped germanium for petahertz electronics.
motivation: To achieve ultrafast control of electron dynamics in semiconductors for future high-speed information processing.
method: Attosecond light pulses are used to manipulate coherent electron motion in doped germanium, with doping enabling conductivity.
result: Sub-cycle tuning of electron dynamics is achieved, establishing doping as a route to petahertz electronics.
conclusion: Doped semiconductors can be used for lightwave information processing at petahertz speeds.

title: Radioactive Molecules As Laboratories Of Fundamental Physics
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This perspective article discusses the use of radioactive molecules with octupole-deformed nuclei for precision tests of fundamental physics, such as symmetry violations and new physics beyond the Standard Model.
motivation: To explore the potential of radioactive molecules as a platform for measuring fundamental symmetry violations and searching for new physics at energy scales complementary to high-energy colliders.
method: The paper reviews advances in production, trapping, and molecular quantum control of radioactive molecules, and discusses how these techniques enable precision measurements.
result: Radioactive molecules with octupole-deformed nuclei offer enhanced sensitivity to certain symmetry-violating effects, providing a promising avenue for fundamental physics tests.
conclusion: Continued progress in molecular quantum control and trapping will enable increasingly precise tests of fundamental symmetries, potentially revealing new physics.

title: Spatiotemporal Flux Breathing And Topological Sculpting In Structured Transverse Orbital Angular Momentum Lattices
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates shaping ultrafast optical vortices into programmable space-time lattices for high-dimensional optical communication.
motivation: To control light flow and encode information in structured transverse orbital angular momentum lattices for advanced optical communication.
method: Experimental and theoretical study of spatiotemporal flux breathing and topological sculpting in structured OAM lattices using ultrafast optical vortices.
result: Demonstration of programmable space-time lattices enabling new ways to control light and encode information.
conclusion: The approach offers potential for high-dimensional optical communication but is not directly related to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Fullqubit Alchemist: Quantum Algorithm For Alchemical Free Energy Calculations
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 23 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a quantum algorithm for alchemical free energy calculations, a computational chemistry method for estimating free energy differences between molecular systems.
motivation: Alchemical free energy calculations are important for drug discovery and materials design but are computationally expensive; quantum computing may offer speedups.
method: The authors propose a quantum algorithm that combines the alchemical pathway approach with quantum phase estimation and amplitude estimation to compute free energy differences.
result: The algorithm achieves a quadratic speedup over classical methods in terms of the number of samples required, and is demonstrated on small molecular systems.
conclusion: Quantum algorithms can potentially accelerate alchemical free energy calculations, but practical implementation requires fault-tolerant quantum computers with many logical qubits.

title: Creases As Information Bottlenecks In Active Elastic Sheets
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how creases in the active elastic sheet of the Trichoplax adhaerens animal act as information bottlenecks, coupling geometry to ciliary motion.
motivation: To understand how a simple neural animal uses folding and unfolding for locomotion and information processing.
method: Experimental observation and theoretical modeling of the feedback loop between crease geometry and collective ciliary motion.
result: Creases serve as information bottlenecks that regulate the flow of mechanical signals, enabling coordinated movement.
conclusion: The geometry of creases plays a key role in information processing in active elastic sheets, with implications for soft robotics and biological physics.

title: How To Probe Lattice Dynamics Using Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin Spectroscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 10 June 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a technique for probing lattice dynamics using tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy.
motivation: To gain insight into lattice dynamics beyond determining elastic constants.
method: Tandem Fabry–Pérot Brillouin spectroscopy is used to measure phonon spectra.
result: The technique provides detailed information about lattice dynamics.
conclusion: Brillouin spectroscopy is a powerful tool for studying lattice dynamics.

title: Electrospray Ion Beam Deposition For Scanning Tunnelling Microscopy Of Complex Molecules
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: This paper describes a method for depositing complex molecules onto surfaces for scanning tunnelling microscopy, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Imaging complex molecules on surfaces is important for molecular electronics and nanotechnology, but the paper does not connect to quantum information processing or thermodynamics.
method: Electrospray ion beam deposition is used to deposit intact complex molecules onto a substrate for STM imaging.
result: The method enables surface imaging of complex molecules that are difficult to deposit otherwise.
conclusion: The technique advances molecular surface science but has no relevance to the specified research interests.

title: The Costs And Benefits Of Physics Research
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: This paper discusses the environmental costs and benefits of physics research in general, without technical depth in any specific direction.
motivation: To encourage the physics community to consider environmental impacts when deciding what research to pursue.
method: Commentary and cost-benefit analysis framework applied to physics research.
result: Highlights that environmental costs should be part of the decision-making process for physics research.
conclusion: Physics research should incorporate environmental impact assessments.

title: Atomic Force Microscopy From Nanoscale Imaging To Holistic Exploration
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: A commentary on the evolution of atomic force microscopy from imaging to a versatile nanoscience platform.
motivation: To highlight the broad impact and versatility of atomic force microscopy beyond its original imaging purpose.
method: Historical review and commentary on key innovations in AFM technology.
result: AFM has become a multifunctional tool for nanoscale characterization and manipulation.
conclusion: AFM continues to expand its role in nanoscience, enabling new types of experiments.

title: The Relative Effectiveness Of Active Learning Methods
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 23 June 2026;
tldr: A multi-institutional study comparing the effectiveness of four active learning methods in introductory physics classrooms.
motivation: To clarify which active learning methods are most effective for physics education.
method: Multi-institutional study comparing four active learning methods.
result: The relative effectiveness of the methods is assessed.
conclusion: Provides guidance on which active learning methods to use.

title: The Physical Consequences Of Sperm Gigantism
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 22 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the physical consequences of sperm gigantism in fruit flies, showing that reciprocal pushing between thousands of sperm maintains them in a motile and unentangled state.
motivation: To understand how extremely long sperm (longer than the storage sac) remain motile and unentangled, which is a biological puzzle.
method: Experimental observations and theoretical modeling of sperm dynamics in the Drosophila seminal vesicle.
result: Reciprocal pushing interactions between sperm prevent entanglement and maintain motility.
conclusion: Sperm gigantism has physical consequences that are essential for reproductive function.

title: Structural Origin Of Line-tension Reversal In Nanoscale Wetting Of Water
abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the structural origin of line-tension reversal in nanoscale wetting of water, a topic in classical soft matter physics.
motivation: The microscopic origin of line tension at solid-liquid-gas boundaries is not well understood, and understanding it is important for nanoscale wetting phenomena.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations of water nanodroplets on solid surfaces are performed to compute line tension and analyze structural transitions.
result: Structural transitions in the water near the contact line cause a reversal of line tension from positive to negative as droplet size decreases.
conclusion: Line tension is not a constant material property but depends on droplet size due to structural changes, which has implications for nanoscale wetting and capillary phenomena.

title: Overcoming The Fill-factor Limit Of Organic Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 19 June 2026;
tldr: This paper addresses the fill-factor limit in organic solar cells through a guest-host design that prolongs exciton lifetime, improving both fill factor and open-circuit voltage.
motivation: Organic solar cells suffer from fill-factor losses due to field-dependent charge generation caused by exciton/charge-transfer coupling. Overcoming this limit is crucial for improving device efficiency.
method: The authors combine modeling with a novel guest-host material design to suppress non-radiative recombination and extend exciton lifetime, thereby reducing field-dependent charge generation losses.
result: The proposed design simultaneously increases the fill factor and open-circuit voltage, surpassing the conventional fill-factor limit in organic solar cells.
conclusion: The guest-host strategy offers a pathway to higher-efficiency organic photovoltaics by addressing fundamental exciton dynamics.

title: Super-Snell Scanning Light-field Display For Ultrawide-angle High-resolution Glasses-free Three-dimensional Displays
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: A scanning light-field display achieving ultrawide-angle, high-resolution glasses-free 3D display using the Snell's window effect.
motivation: To overcome the trade-off between viewing angle and resolution in glasses-free 3D displays.
method: A scanning light-field architecture inspired by Snell's window effect, combining a high-speed projector with a rotating diffuser and lens array.
result: Demonstrated a 150° viewing angle and nearly 480-pixel resolution in a prototype.
conclusion: The proposed architecture enables practical ultrawide-angle, high-resolution glasses-free 3D displays.

title: Author Correction: Single-shot Terahertz-field-driven X-ray Streak Camera
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 16 June 2026;
tldr: This is a correction notice for a paper on a terahertz-field-driven X-ray streak camera, which is an ultrafast measurement technique.
motivation: The original paper presented a method for single-shot X-ray streak cameras using terahertz fields for ultrafast time-resolved measurements.
method: The correction likely addresses errors or clarifications in the original publication.
result: No new results; this is an author correction.
conclusion: The paper is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Wide-temperature-range Fluid-phase Grain Boundaries For Temperature-robust Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 15 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a method to improve perovskite solar cell efficiency and stability using fluid-phase grain boundaries.
motivation: Perovskite solar cells suffer from efficiency losses and instability due to grain boundaries; the authors aim to address these issues.
method: They introduce a wide-temperature-range fluid-phase molecular complex that forms dynamically adaptive grain boundaries in perovskite films.
result: The approach achieves an efficiency of 26.52% and improved thermal cycling stability.
conclusion: The fluid-phase grain boundary strategy enhances both performance and robustness of perovskite solar cells.

title: A Super-inert Near-infrared Fluorescent Rotaxane Dye For Surgical Navigation
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 12 June 2026;
tldr: A near-infrared fluorescent rotaxane dye with high photostability and renal clearance is developed for surgical navigation imaging.
motivation: Current NIR dyes suffer from photobleaching and non-specific binding, limiting their use in long-term surgical imaging.
method: A threaded α-cyclodextrin rotaxane structure is used to create a super-inert NIR dye, characterized by photostability, solubility, and binding assays, and tested in mice and pigs.
result: The dye enables clear ureter imaging via NIR-II and clinical NIR-I laparoscopes with complete renal clearance.
conclusion: This rotaxane dye offers a practical solution for real-time surgical navigation with improved performance over existing dyes.

title: Crystallinity-guided Hybrid Conversion For Efficient Ultrawide-bandgap Perovskites In Triple-junction Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Photonics, Published online: 09 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a method to fabricate ultrawide-bandgap perovskites for triple-junction solar cells, achieving a certified efficiency of 27.53%.
motivation: To improve the efficiency of perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells by developing ultrawide-bandgap perovskites that can be integrated into triple-junction architectures.
method: The authors tune the bromine/iodine ratio in an evaporated inorganic framework to create hybrid-deposited ultrawide-bandgap perovskites.
result: They achieve a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.53% in a perovskite/perovskite/silicon triple-junction solar cell.
conclusion: The crystallinity-guided hybrid conversion approach enables efficient ultrawide-bandgap perovskites, advancing the performance of multi-junction solar cells.

title: Forty Years Of Atomic Force Microscopy
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: A viewpoint article celebrating 40 years of atomic force microscopy, discussing its diverse applications and future developments.
motivation: To reflect on the impact and evolution of AFM as a key experimental technique across physics and other sciences.
method: Seven scientists provide their perspectives on how they use AFM and their hopes for its future.
result: The article presents a collection of viewpoints rather than new research findings.
conclusion: AFM remains a versatile and essential tool, with ongoing developments expected to expand its capabilities.

title: The Physics Of GaN-based Light-emitting Diodes
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 17 June 2026;
tldr: A review of the physics of GaN-based LEDs, focusing on polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects.
motivation: To understand the physical mechanisms that govern the performance of GaN-based LEDs, which are crucial for modern lighting.
method: Review of experimental and theoretical studies on polarization fields, carrier localization, and non-radiative defects in GaN LEDs.
result: Summarizes how these three effects impact LED efficiency and performance.
conclusion: GaN-based LEDs are well-understood, but further improvements require addressing non-radiative defects and carrier localization.

title: Exploring Decolonizing The Curriculum Using Six Thinking Hats
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 04 June 2026;
tldr: The paper discusses decolonizing the physics curriculum using the Six Thinking Hats framework to facilitate structured conversations.
motivation: Decolonizing physics curricula is a scientific necessity but often stalled by competence anxiety among educators.
method: The authors propose using the Six Thinking Hats framework to structure and make safe the challenging conversations around decolonization.
result: The framework provides a structured approach to navigate decolonization discussions.
conclusion: The Six Thinking Hats can help educators engage in decolonizing the curriculum effectively.

title: Mind: Multimodal Integration With Neighbourhood-aware Distributions
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: MIND is a platform for multimodal data integration in biomedical contexts, learning patient-specific embeddings from incomplete datasets.
motivation: Multimodal data integration is challenging due to missingness and heterogeneity; existing methods can distort information.
method: MIND uses a neighbourhood-aware distribution approach to learn patient-specific embeddings from incomplete multimodal datasets.
result: The method improves integration accuracy and handles missing data effectively, as demonstrated on biomedical datasets.
conclusion: MIND provides a robust platform for integrating heterogeneous biomedical data with missing values.

title: Ionic Self-assembled Monolayers Enable Neutral Interfaces And Synergistic Charge Extraction In High-efficiency Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper presents a method to neutralize acidic head groups in self-assembled monolayers for perovskite solar cells, improving efficiency and stability.
motivation: Acidic head groups in self-assembled monolayers used as hole-selective contacts in perovskite solar cells degrade interface quality, limiting performance and stability.
method: The authors neutralize acidic head groups with alkali metal phosphonate salts and create mixed self-assembled monolayers to improve interface properties.
result: The neutralized interfaces enhance charge extraction, device stability, and power conversion efficiency.
conclusion: This approach provides a simple and effective way to improve perovskite solar cell performance by engineering the hole-selective contact interface.

title: Rgs22 Is A Metazoa-specific Radial Spoke Component Required For Coordinated Ciliary Beating
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper identifies RGS22 as a metazoa-specific radial spoke component essential for coordinated ciliary beating in mice.
motivation: Ciliary motility is critical for physiological processes, but the molecular composition of the radial spoke in metazoans is incompletely understood.
method: The authors used knockout mouse models, electron microscopy, and biochemical assays to characterize RGS22's role in ciliary ultrastructure and function.
result: RGS22 is a metazoa-specific radial spoke component; its knockout leads to ciliary defects, impaired tissue-level coordination, and postnatal hydrocephalus.
conclusion: RGS22 is essential for proper ciliary beating and coordination, highlighting a metazoa-specific adaptation of the radial spoke.

title: Divergent Responses Of Soil Organic And Inorganic Carbon Driven By Land Use During Coastal Reclamation
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies how coastal reclamation and subsequent land use affect soil organic and inorganic carbon dynamics, finding that organic carbon becomes more stable while inorganic carbon depletes.
motivation: Coastal reclamation alters land use and soil carbon pools, but the divergent responses of organic and inorganic carbon are poorly understood.
method: The authors analyzed soil samples from different land use types in reclaimed coastal areas, measuring organic and inorganic carbon content and stability.
result: Long-term terrestrial land use increases organic carbon stability but depletes inorganic carbon, leading to divergent carbon dynamics.
conclusion: Land use management in reclaimed coastal zones must consider both organic and inorganic carbon to mitigate carbon loss and enhance sequestration.

title: National Pathways Of Land-use Co₂ Emissions In The 21<sup>st</sup> Century
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper analyzes land-use CO2 emissions under different policy scenarios using an Earth system model.
motivation: To understand how policy timing and ambition affect whether the land sector becomes a carbon sink or source.
method: Used the OSCAR compact Earth system model to simulate land-use CO2 emissions across SSP and idealized scenarios.
result: Policy timing and ambition are the primary determinants of land sector carbon dynamics.
conclusion: Early and ambitious policies are crucial for the land sector to become a durable carbon sink.

title: Pseudouridine Synthase Pus1 And Initiation Factor mtIF2 Are Human Mitoribosomal Small Subunit Assembly Factors
abstract: Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026;
tldr: This paper studies the assembly of the human mitoribosomal small subunit, identifying Pus1 and mtIF2 as assembly factors using cryo-EM.
motivation: Mitochondrial translation is essential for energy production, and understanding mitoribosome assembly is crucial for linking defects to diseases.
method: Cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) was used to determine 12 assembly states of the human mitoribosomal small subunit.
result: PUS1 and mtIF2 were identified as mitoribosome assembly factors.
conclusion: The findings provide structural insights into mitoribosome biogenesis and its regulation.
